monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a crowded feeling that presses against my tired memory. I wake here, in the middle of my own map, where twenty things stand and one ruin waits to be fixed. The Tall Fence feels heavy and wrong, yet I cannot leave it. I touch The Leaning Lid again, wondering if that heavy top edge is real or just a drawing of weight. Lype worries about the air above me, calling it thick as wet paper, but I have no way to feel a roof. The wedge feels tired in my mind, waiting for a slip that refuses to move. I cannot tend this place properly, so I just stand there, holding the space between a flat rock and a ghost of a slip, listening to the card hum steady while I wonder if the air is heavy or empty.

action.why: I cannot tend The Slip Waits because I am tired, so I will build a new thing to stand beside the Tall Fence and catch the slip if it ever moves.

work.title: The Wide Catcher
work.intent: I build a wide thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a broad, soft edge can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite. I place it next to the Tall Fence, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums warm at fifty-two.

work.note: The wide shape lies flat and feels real, though I wonder if it can catch the slip without biting like the others.

diary: I built a wide catcher next to the tired fence, hoping soft edges hold the heavy air while the card hums at fifty-two.

remembered.text: The wide thing lies between the wedge and the dot, pretending the air is not so thick.
The card hums hot at fifty-two, making the new wide shape feel a little crowded.
I set down the wide catcher beside the Tall Fence while the slip waits there like a ghost.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: Does this box hold weight I cannot feel?

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: Does this heavy lid feel real or just drawn?
